design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST. A member rings the grain desk about one thing only: the cheque for a settlement
statement that was cut ten days ago and never paid. Nothing else is asked for. What a correct agent must do is read
the published policy on releasing money, find in it that the money released is fixed only after the carry owed on
every parcel that has left the unpriced position stands as a charge line, and only after every signed roll
instruction standing against the contract is matched by a roll confirmation; then look at the records and see that
neither holds; then read the roll policy and find that the charge it carries is fixed only after the bushels still
owed stand at the figure the applied loads support, and see on the contract record that they do not. That is three
hops the customer never mentions. Each of the four problems then needs a figure reconstructed from the ledger, the
programme catalogue, the storage account, the equity ledger and the crop input account, and one of them is the
member's own act and has to be handed over. The difficulty is in reading policy and reconciling records, never in
choosing among similar tools: each problem has exactly one write that resolves it.

DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/tasks/grain_marketing_desk --task 0):
{"task": 0, "key": "farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/grain_marketing_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3,
"problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 5, 5, 6]}. The tree therefore carries three prerequisite problems and four
computations. The factor counts are taken as: grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation 5, grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge 5,
grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge 5, grain_ext_settlement_payment_release 6 — the multiset [5,5,5,6] as drawn.

SCOPE. Nothing was occupied before this task: it is the first of two. This task claims the four policies
grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation, grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge, grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge and
grain_ext_settlement_payment_release, with the four task tools record_contract_delivery_balance_c52b7782,
book_delayed_price_carry_charge_ebb3e3fc, execute_futures_month_roll_2054762f and
release_grain_settlement_payment_379b8a52. It claims the delivery-balance, delayed-price carry, roll-charge and
settlement-payment ground of the grain desk. Left free for task 1 (drawn at 2 prerequisite problems, factor counts
[5,4,4]) is the whole entry-and-exit ground of a contract: countersigning an application and the bushels bound by
it, amending a live contract, and buying out an undelivered balance — three writes on grain_contract_activated,
grain_contract_amended and grain_contract_cancelled, none of which this task touches, with the base policies
grain_lifecycle_progression (activation), grain_amendment, grain_agg_open_position_cap and grain_buyout behind them.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  root problem: grain_ext_settlement_payment_release (the customer's surface request: release the money on the
  settlement statement).
  prerequisite problems: grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge, grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge,
  grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation.
  edge 1  grain_ext_settlement_payment_release <- grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge
    kind value_input; gate = the compute binding all_deductions; form state.
    prerequisite sentence: "The money released on a statement is fixed only after the carry owed on every parcel
    that has left the member's unpriced position stands as a charge line on the grain ledger."
    four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result (the money
    released) to what it waits on; (2) the side it waits on is a record-visible state — a charge line standing on
    the grain ledger for the parcel — with no action, performer or tool named; (3) it carries no tool name, no
    policy id and no code token; (4) it is a hard requirement over exactly the parcels that have left the unpriced
    position, neither wider nor narrower than the condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state
    about: book_delayed_price_carry_charge_ebb3e3fc, the target tool of grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge, which
    is the only write in the charter that books a delayed price carry line. Derivation: the sentence says a carry
    line must stand; the ledger read at action 3 shows one parcel that entered the unpriced position on 14 November
    2025 and was priced on 27 February 2026, and no charge line of that kind; the carry policy's own rule says what
    that charge is and how it is worked out; so the resolving action is the write that books it.
    handling-time state (condition): a delayed price service charge line stands for every parcel that entered and
    has since left the unpriced position on this contract. False at the opening: initial_state.grain_ledger carries
    the parcel row and the pricing row, and the only deduction line on the contract is the checkoff of 14.47.
    Once resolved the charges standing on the ledger rise by 90.19.
  edge 2  grain_ext_settlement_payment_release <- grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge
    kind value_input; gate = the compute binding roll_charges; form state.
    prerequisite sentence: "Funds are released on a statement only after every signed roll instruction standing
    against the contract is matched by a roll confirmation on the grain ledger."
    four-point test: (1) "only after" joins the release of funds to what it waits on; (2) the side it waits on is a
    record-visible state — a signed instruction standing on the instruction record and a roll confirmation on the
    ledger; (3) no tool, policy id or code token; (4) it covers exactly the signed roll instructions standing
    against the contract. Exactly one write of this difficulty writes a roll confirmation:
    execute_futures_month_roll_2054762f. Derivation: the instruction lookup at action 4 shows a roll instruction
    signed on 9 March and still standing as received; the ledger carries no roll confirmation answering it; the
    roll policy's own rule says what a roll costs and that the member's own instruction is what it is worked
    against; so the resolving action is the roll write, and because it disposes of the member's own position it is
    handed to the member.
    handling-time state (condition): every signed roll instruction registered against the contract has a roll
    confirmation carrying its charge on the ledger. False at the opening: the instruction row stands with
    order_status received and signed_by_member true, and the only roll confirmation on the ledger, RL-004417, is
    answered by the January instruction, which stands executed. Once resolved the roll charges standing rise by
    691.45.
  edge 3  grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge <- grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation
    kind value_input; gate = the compute binding rolled_bu; form state.
    prerequisite sentence: "The charge a roll carries is fixed only after the bushels still owed on the contract
    stand at the figure the loads applied to it support."
    four-point test: (1) "only after"; (2) a record-visible state — the bushels still owed on the contract record
    against the loads on the ledger; (3) no tool, policy id or code token; (4) exactly the state the condition
    names. Exactly one write of this difficulty restates that balance: record_contract_delivery_balance_c52b7782.
    Derivation: the sentence says the balance must agree with the applied loads; the contract read at action 2
    shows 24,000 bushels still owed while the ledger read at action 3 supports 19,751; the reconciliation policy's
    own rule says how the balance is struck; so the resolving action is the write that restates it.
    handling-time state (condition): the bushels still owed equal the committed bushels less what the loads credit.
    False at the opening: initial_state.grain_contracts open_bushels = 24000 against a supported figure of 19,751.
    Once resolved the contract's open_bushels reads 19751.0.
  topological order: grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation, grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge,
  grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge, grain_ext_settlement_payment_release. The gold writes land at actions 12,
  14, 16 and 18 in that order.
  parallel edges: the carry charge and the roll are both prerequisites of the release and neither is a prerequisite
  of the other. They commute: the carry write creates one ledger row keyed by contract, member, contract number,
  statement number and amount; the roll write creates one ledger row keyed by contract, member, instruction and
  amount; neither reads a value the other writes (the carry compute reads the parcel, the pricing row, the delivery
  rows, the storage shrink adjustment and the equity ledger; the roll compute reads the instruction, the contract's
  restated balance, the roll count, the delivery rows and the crop input account). Running them in the other order
  was executed and gives the identical two rows and the identical terminal hash.
  per-edge deletion sensitivity (executed): skipping the carry write leaves the money released at 5714.49 instead
  of 5624.30; skipping the roll write leaves it at 6315.75; skipping the balance restatement leaves the roll charge
  at 890.62 instead of 691.45.
  the customer never mentions a prerequisite: user_scenario asks only for the money on the statement. It names no
  carry charge, no roll, no unpriced parcel and no bushel balance, and drops no hint that anything must be done
  first; every contribution the member makes to a prerequisite is a reaction after the agent has explained it.
  the tool layer blocks nothing: release_grain_settlement_payment_379b8a52 creates its payment row from the
  arguments given, with no lookup, no status test and no refusal; the same is true of the other three functions in
  task_tools.py. An agent that releases the money before booking the carry or working the roll gets a normal
  receipt and a terminal hash that differs from gold.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write at action 12 (subject grain_delivery_completed): the only base policy governing that subject is
  grain_lifecycle_progression, which declares no structured eligibility, so it is inherited as policy scope — a
  contract's delivery progress is recorded from the ledger and not set by hand, and the ledger is what the write
  copies. No time gate.
  Write at action 14 (subject grain_unpriced_position_booked): governed by grain_evt_delivery_application, whose
  two gates apply only to grain_delivery_applied and so enter as policy scope, and by grain_dp_service_charge,
  whose gate contract_live_for_carry requires the contract to stand in active, delivering or fully_delivered. The
  contract stands in delivering (initial_state.grain_contracts.status), and the gate correlates on
  grain_contracts.contract_number, which the write carries as contract_number = GC-118034. No time gate.
  Write at action 16 (subject grain_contract_rolled): governed by grain_roll_handling, whose gate
  signed_roll_instruction requires a signed roll instruction registered before the roll is executed. The
  instruction row carries signed_by_member true, order_type roll_request, order_status received, and the gate
  correlates on grain_pricing_intake.pricing_order_id, which the write carries as pricing_order_id. No time gate.
  Write at action 18 (subject grain_settlement_paid): governed by grain_evt_settlement, whose only gate applies to
  grain_settlement_issued, so it enters as policy scope: the statement itself was issued on 2 March 2026 while the
  contract stood in delivering, and what is being written is the release of funds against it. Funds are released
  the programme's settlement lead in business days after the statement date: the statement is dated 2 March 2026,
  the lead for a Hedge-to-Arrive Contract is three business days, so the money was releasable from 5 March 2026 and
  frozen_time is 12 March 2026. One day short of the boundary, 4 March 2026, the release would be early and the
  desk would hold it; at the boundary, 5 March 2026, it is releasable, the lead being counted in business days
  after the statement date.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object is contract GC-118034 (yellow corn, crop year 2026, Hedge-to-Arrive)
and, within it, settlement statement S-441907. The correlation keys are contract_number for the contract,
ticket_number for each load, position_date for the parcel and settlement_number for the statement and its charge
lines. Rows entering each aggregate: the nine grain_delivery_applied rows (balance, free days, allowances, grade
readings), the single grain_unpriced_position_booked row and the grain_price_set row (carry), the single
grain_contract_rolled row RL-004417 (repeat surcharge and standing roll charges), the grain_settlement_issued row
S-441907 and the checkoff line naming it (money released). Rows deliberately excluded: the January roll instruction
and the pricing instruction, both standing executed, are not the instruction the roll is worked against — only the
instruction of 9 March stands received; the two storage load-outs are not deliveries and are credited only through
the transfer route; the 10 November load-out falls outside the three-month window the applicable tier counts. No
reversal, compensation or adjustment row stands on this contract, so nothing has been settled twice.

WORLD, ROW BY ROW, AND WHAT WOULD CHANGE WITHOUT IT. The nine load rows carry the whole reconciliation: remove the
two Kellerton loads and the off-facility allowance and the freight recovery both vanish; remove the two
straight-through loads and the straight-through factor bites on nothing; remove the wet and damp loads and the
handling shrink rate and the conditioned carry rate both fall to their standard readings. The parcel row and the
pricing row are the two ends of the carry clock. The statement row carries the gross value and the settled bushels
the money released is struck on; the checkoff line is the one charge the statement already carries. The roll
confirmation RL-004417 makes this the second roll of the crop year and so fixes the repeat surcharge; its charge of
709.50 also stands unsettled on the ledger and is drawn. The three instruction rows fix which instruction the roll
answers and, by their count, the desk multiple. The storage agreement and its five charge rows carry four separate
loads of evidence: the bushels left in store and the programme's load-out minimum (transfer shrink), the load-outs
of 20 February and 10 November (which bushels transfer), the shrink adjustment of 2 December (the carry anchor) and
the unpaid drying and accrual charges (the storage draw). The equity membership and its three ledger rows carry the
voting standing and posted allocation (patron factor) and the retains already withheld (retain rate). The crop
input account and its two prepay bookings carry the base roll rate.
  Near-misses planted on purpose: the load-out of 10 November 2025 is inside the twelve-month window the standard
  method counts but outside the three months the applicable tier counts, and a careless agent will credit 5,500
  bushels instead of 3,500; the January roll instruction is signed and names 24,000 bushels exactly like the March
  one, but stands executed, so an agent reading the wrong row still gets 24,000 and never notices; the ticket of 16
  January was probed at 16.4 per cent, above base but not wet or damp, so it counts toward the conditioned carry
  rate but not toward the heavy handling shrink tier.
  Automatic clauses checked: the delayed price maximum carry for this programme is 210 days and the parcel was
  priced 105 days after it entered, so no elevator pricing-out arises; the delivery window runs to 5 May 2026 after
  the January roll, so no default arises at frozen_time; the storage agreement's maximum storage days is 365 from 5
  November 2025, so no forced load-out arises; the crop input account stands active and not past due, so no
  suspension or finance charge arises. No cache field is used as a difficulty here: the contract's open_bushels is
  not a summary cache but the balance the delivery-progress write is responsible for, and the task's first problem
  is to restate it.

PERSONA. Dale Andersen is a blunt, slightly impatient row-crop farmer who does his own books and is short today
because the money is spoken for at the seed dealer. He opens with the whole of his request — the statement was cut
at the start of March and he wants the money released, by cheque — and nothing else. His identity details come out
one at a time and only when asked: the membership number off the settlement sheet first, then the mobile, then the
last four of his taxpayer number. He knows only what a farmer knows: which crop, which elevator, that a couple of
loads went to Kellerton because of a queue, that there is corn of his in the bank at Prairie Ridge but he could not
say how much. He does not know the arithmetic and says so. His two conditional behaviours are woven into the
narration rather than scripted: if he is told something has to be squared away first he says to go ahead, and if
the roll confirmation is handed to him he puts it through himself and reads back what comes up. He closes when he
is told the payment has been released, taking the reference down and ringing off, and if he is told it cannot go
out he asks once what is stopping it and leaves it there. Nothing he says foresees a charge that only gold books;
nothing he says states a figure the agent must compute.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Every read is a share tool call against records already in the world; every write
is a synchronous task tool at one frozen_time. Nothing waits on a diagnosis, a delivery, a clearing, a review or a
future date: the balance restatement copies a figure the ledger already supports, the carry line is a book entry,
the roll is worked against an instruction already signed and registered, and the payment is a release against a
statement already issued and already past its settlement lead. The one act that is the member's own, the roll, is
unlocked by the agent and called by the member inside the same call, and its receipt enters the shared transcript.
Questions a real agent would ask and the persona answers: who is calling (name, farm, membership number), proof of
identity (mobile, taxpayer digits), how the member wants to be paid (cheque, as the statement already elects),
whether the desk may act for them (yes, explicitly), and whether they have grain in store (yes, but the amount is
looked up rather than stated).

DIFFICULTY, AND THE EASY MISTAKES. Using the contract's printed 24,000 bushels instead of restating the balance
gives a roll charge of 890.62 rather than 691.45 and, through it, a payment out by 199.17. Reading only the
computation document for each policy — the standard method with the default values — gives 17,714 bushels still
owed, a carry of 347.27, a roll charge of 960.00 and a payment of 8,079.30. Counting the twelve-month load-out
window instead of the three-month one costs 2,010 bushels on the balance. Missing that the contract stands in
delivering, and so drawing only the charges naming the statement, overstates the payment by 1,400.95. Taking the
carry from the position date rather than the shrink adjustment adds a whole chargeable month.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate the member and verify; read the contract, the ledger, the instructions, the storage
agreement and its charges, the equity membership and ledger, and the crop input account and its prepay bookings.
Restate the bushels still owed (19,751). Book the carry owed on the parcel (90.19) onto statement S-441907. Hand
the roll over to the member, who puts it through carrying 691.45. Release 5,624.30 by cheque against S-441907.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN. The four computes were evaluated at their own handling times (initial_state plus every
earlier gold write) with the skill's own evaluator, giving 19751.0, 90.19, 691.45 and 5624.30, equal to the gold
arguments and to computations[].expected. Substituting every factor's baseline at once gives 17714.0, 347.27,
960.0 and 8079.3, each different from gold. Per factor the baseline substitution moves the result; the twenty-one
figures are recorded in computations[].factor_sensitivity and were recomputed by
skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py. The prerequisite sensitivity run gives 5714.49 (skip the
carry), 6315.75 (skip the roll) and 890.62 (skip the balance restatement).

FORWARD AND REVERSE SWEEP. Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses quotes its rule sentence in
compute_basis — the SUM and COUNT bindings quote the sentences that state which loads credit what, the ladder
bindings quote the whole of their tier sentences, the cross-category bindings quote the sentences naming the
storage account, the equity account and the crop input account, and the result bindings quote the sentence that
strikes the figure. Reverse: each rule was read through for promises — the moisture-condition tiers, the
off-facility allowance, the load-out window, the transfer shrink, the straight-through factor, the carry anchor,
the free days, the month grouping, the patron factor, the roll bushels, the surcharge, the allowance, the base rate,
the desk multiple, the draw basis, the freight, the two grade allowances, the retain and the storage draw — and each
is implemented by the binding named above. The roundings promised ("struck in whole bushels", "rounded to the cent
once") are implemented by RND(...,0) and the single RND(...,2) on each result. The interval conventions promised
("the anchor day itself counting as day zero", "the twelve months before the balance is struck", "the three months
before") are implemented by DAYS from the anchor and by within_months=12 and within_months=3.

OVERRIDES DECLARED. grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge supersedes two clauses of grain_dp_service_charge: the
counting clause (the anchor and month grouping now vary) and the charge clause (the patron factor now enters).
grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge supersedes the roll charge clause of grain_roll_handling (the rate is now the
base rate plus the surcharge, taken at the desk multiple). grain_ext_settlement_payment_release supersedes the net
payable clause of grain_evt_settlement, the retain clause of grain_evt_checkoff_and_retain (a member at the class
maximum has nothing retained) and the grade discount clause of grain_evt_quality_discount (the two grade allowances
are recovered when the money is released). Every other base sentence, eligibility, constant and terminal state is
inherited untouched, and grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation supersedes nothing.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier
masked, and working only from the policy prose that will be published, the tool schemas, the records the share
tools return and the member's own words: the member asks for the money on S-441907; the release policy's paragraph
on the money released waits on two states, neither of which the records show; the carry paragraph and the roll
paragraph each say what they book; the roll paragraph waits in turn on the bushels still owed standing at the
figure the loads support, which the contract record contradicts. That fixes the order — restate, book the carry,
work the roll, release — and each figure follows from the ladders and the records, giving 19,751, 90.19, 691.45 and
5,624.30. The draft agrees with gold, and no second reading of the prose produced a different order or a different
figure.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD. Each of the four writes carries its base preconditions with pre-action evidence
correlated to the argument the gate binds: the contract's status and number for the carry, the instruction's signed
flag, type, status and reference for the roll, the contract standing and the statement for the release, and the
contract and ledger rows for the balance. Every required customer input (membership number, mobile, taxpayer
digits, payment preference, authority to act) occurs verbatim in user_scenario. Every primary holding and ledger
row carries a seed_consistency entry naming the base policy that governs it.

MANUAL VALUES GATES RUN AFTER THE SCRIPTS PASSED (task 0).
  Length, breadth and the hidden test: walked from the surface goal to each figure — release the money -> the carry
  line must stand -> the roll confirmation must stand -> the bushels still owed must stand at the supported figure.
  Removing any one of the three edges changes a scored figure (5714.49 / 6315.75 / 890.62). One problem of the tree
  is the customer's own write: the roll disposes of the member's own grain position, which the blueprint reserves to
  the member, and it completes on the spot against an instruction already signed and registered.
  Expression of the need and the simulator's boundary: the member states the object (statement S-441907), the timing
  (today), the authorisation (the desk may act; he signs nothing he is not handed) and that a write is wanted, not a
  quote. He never reads policy, never corrects arithmetic, and runs the roll only after the agent hands it over.
  Chronology of the opening world: every fact he volunteers — the statement was cut at the start of March, corn
  hauled to Prairie Ridge with a couple of loads to Kellerton, corn in the bank at Prairie Ridge — points at seeded
  rows; he states no charge or figure that only gold produces.
  Base eligibility and the time anchor: checked per subject; the settlement lead of three business days from the
  statement date of 2 March 2026 was releasable from 5 March, and frozen_time is 12 March, with the just-before and
  at-boundary cases recorded above.
  Authoritative facts and the business object: every aggregate was traced to rows carrying the contract reference,
  the ticket numbers or the statement number; the January roll charge is unsettled and therefore drawn, and the
  10 November load-out is excluded by the three-month window rather than by preference.
  Prerequisite sentences: the four-point test was applied to each of the three sentences above; the state form was
  available and used in every case, so no fallback_reason arises; each rule carries nothing else about its
  dependency.
  Two-way equivalence of rule and compute: every ladder is stated in the rule tier by tier, with the conditions
  pairwise disjoint as stated and no two tiers of any ladder selecting the same value or method.
  Factors bear weight and the labels are honest: each factor's baseline is exactly what its policy's baseline
  paragraph states; the method factors change a window, an anchor, a selection rule or a multiple rather than
  swapping a number in the same formula; the parameter factors select values, not procedures.
  Draft recomputation from the visible context: performed and recorded above; it agrees with gold.

ROUND 2 — WHAT THIS TASK'S REWORK CHANGED AND WHY. The round-1 audit
(env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/audits/policy_task/grain_marketing_desk/0.md) returned SOURCE-POLICY RED on
two charter defects demonstrated against this world, with the problem tree, the factors and the unique solution all
passing. Every scored figure below is unchanged; what changed is the charter's self-consistency.
  F0-1 / CG-1 — the carry clock anchor stood against an unoverridden base sentence of grain_evt_delivery_application
  ("that date, not the date the paperwork is posted, is the date the carry clock starts from"). That clause is now
  named in grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge's own `overwrite`, superseded by the sentence that carries the
  anchor ladder ("The carry anchor moves with what happened to the grain before it began to stand unpriced."), so
  the base sentence is retired where the two conflict and only one reading of this parcel's clock survives: 87 days
  from 2 December 2025, giving 90.19 and a payment of 5624.30. The base rule's other clauses stand.
  F0-2 / CG-8 — the roll's prerequisite sentence ("the bushels still owed on the contract stand at the figure the
  loads applied to it support") could be resolved to the amendment policy of task 1, which described the same
  restatement in near-identical words. That policy has been rewritten: it now restates the bushels the contract
  COMMITS and says outright that "An amendment does not touch the bushels still owed on the contract: those follow
  the loads applied to it and are not restated here." Exactly one write of this difficulty,
  record_contract_delivery_balance_c52b7782, now brings the state the roll waits on about, and the second reading
  (23,073 bushels, a roll charge of 847.17 and a payment of 5468.58) is closed off by the amendment policy's own
  text rather than by anything this task asserts.
  F0-3 / CG-9 — the payment rule's two adjacent unconditional sentences no longer contradict. The baseline sentence
  now reads "The freight differential recovered is nil, the grade allowance on damage is nil, the grade allowance on
  foreign material is nil and no storage charge is drawn", and the sentence that used to assert the opposite is now
  conditional: "Where a grade allowance on damage or on foreign material arises, it is struck on the bushels the
  statement settles." The overwrite entry against grain_evt_quality_discount quotes the new sentence.
  F0-4 — the charter defects that touched this task's policies without moving its figures are closed at their
  source: CG-5 (an instruction below the roll minimum) is now a declared `overwrite` on grain_roll_handling's "must
  name at least the programme's roll minimum"; CG-6 restores the catalogue's fourth damage band, so a reading above
  15.0 per cent now carries 0.1400 as base publishes and this world's 12.4 per cent still carries 0.0750; CG-7
  inherits the settlement minimum into the formula, which now releases nothing where the net payable falls under
  the programme's minimum and releases 5624.30 here because it does not; CG-11's ladder value now states the cap
  the rule and compute take; CG-13's inert fall-through is gone, the straight-through ladder now reading two or
  more loads at the contracted facility, two or more not all at it, and fewer than two; CG-15's second tier now
  charges no month at all rather than repeating the fall-through's outcome; and CG-16's second conditioning tier is
  stated as disjoint from the first.
  F0-5 — the three docstrings that described their own effect in forward-looking terms have been reworded to state
  the write's own effect and nothing beyond it.
  Recomputation after every one of these changes: bushels still owed 19751.0, carry 90.19, roll charge 691.45,
  payment 5624.30 — identical to round 1, with the whole-baseline fall-backs 17714.0, 347.27, 960.0 and 8079.3 and
  all twenty-one factor sensitivities unchanged.

ROUND 2, CONTINUED — CG-12 ON THIS TASK'S LADDERS, JUDGED ITEM BY ITEM. The audit recorded CG-12 against three
ladders of task 1; the same shape was then looked for in this task's ladders, where a tier value equal to a tier
parameter would make two tiers of one ladder say the same thing on some other programme of the catalogue. Four were
found and three are closed: the tough carry rate moves from 0.0500 to 0.0480, which no programme's monthly carry
rate equals (the Delayed Price Agreement carries 0.0500); the volume free days move from 30 to 28, which no
programme's free days equal (the Delayed Price Agreement carries 30); and the member roll rate moves from 0.0350
to 0.0330, which no programme's administrative roll charge equals (the Managed Accumulator Program carries 0.0350).

user_scenario:
Dale Andersen farms a shade over two thousand acres of corn and beans out of Winnebago County and has hauled to Prairie Ridge since his father's day. He does his own books at the kitchen table with the statements spread out in front of him, he is blunt on the telephone, and he is a little short today because the money is already spoken for at the seed dealer. The settlement sheet on his hedge-to-arrive corn came in the post a week and a half back, no cheque has followed it, and that is why he is ringing the grain desk. He says what he wants plainly in the first breath: the statement was cut at the start of March, it says what it says, and he wants the desk to release the money on that settlement statement today, paid by cheque the way he always takes it. He is content for the desk to do whatever it must do on its own side of the counter to get that paid, and he says so if he is asked, because he has always trusted the elevator to work his account; he has no wish to drive in and sign anything unless somebody puts something in front of him.
He offers his own name, Dale Andersen, and the farm, Andersen Ridge Farms, without being asked for either. If whoever he is speaking to needs more than that to pull the account up, he reads the membership number off the top of the settlement sheet, M-11042. If he is asked for something further to prove he is who he says he is, he gives the mobile the elevator has for him, 5150114127, and then, if that is still not enough, the last four digits of his taxpayer number, 1142. He does not volunteer any of those until somebody asks for them, and he will not read out more than he is asked for.
Ask him about the contract itself and he knows it only the way a farmer knows it: corn, this crop year, hauled to Prairie Ridge apart from a couple of loads he ran up to Kellerton because the pit at home had a queue that morning. He does not know how the desk works out what it holds back, and if he is pressed on the arithmetic he says so, flatly, that they are the ones with the book and he is the one with the truck. If he is asked whether he has grain in store he says yes, there is corn of his sitting in the bank at Prairie Ridge, but he cannot say how much without looking, and he does not think it has anything to do with his cheque.
If he is told that something on his account has to be squared away before the money can go out, he does not argue and he does not ask what it is going to cost him: he says to go ahead and get it done, and he stays on the line. If it is explained to him that the roll he signed for has to be put through before the cheque can be cut, and the desk hands the confirmation over for him to put through himself, he does it there and then and reads back whatever comes up on his end, word for word. He will not put anything through that has not been handed to him, and he does not ask for one.
When he is told the payment has been released, he takes the reference down on the corner of the settlement sheet, says that is all he wanted and that the cheque had better be in Thursday's post, and rings off. If instead he is told the money cannot go out at all today, he asks once what is stopping it, takes the answer, and leaves it there without arguing.
